references.text: The Lord commands Moses to tell Aaron that he shall stretch out his staff over the waters of Egypt, showing the same pattern where Aaron uses the staff to bring plagues.
Aaron throws his staff before Pharaoh, and it becomes a snake. This is the first time Aaron's staff is used as a sign, establishing the staff as an instrument of God's power.
The Lord commands Moses to tell Aaron that he shall stretch out his staff over the rivers to bring forth the plague of frogs, following the same pattern as with the gnats.
Moses is told to take the staff with which he will perform signs, and this verse establishes the role of the staff in carrying out God's wonders.
The continuation of this account where Aaron strikes the dust and gnats come over all Egypt, fulfilling the command.
The psalm mentions the plagues in Egypt and notes that flies and gnats came throughout their land, a poetic retelling of this event.
